technology.title: Bicycle Hub Key Specifications
technology.intro: Understanding the core specifications of your hubs is critical for wheel building and frame compatibility.

jBend.title: J-Bend (Classic)
items: Spoke head is bent (elbow) to fit the flange.
Pros: Easy to service, with replacement spokes widely available.
Cons: Traditional look, with stress concentration at the elbow.

straightPull.title: Straight-Pull (Modern)
items: Spokes are straight, with no elbow.
Pros: Higher tension potential and a sleek aesthetic.
Cons: Harder to find specific replacements on the road.

axle.title: Axle Standards
axle.note: Thru-axles (12mm/15mm) provide superior stiffness compared to Quick Release.

brake.title: Brake Interface
brake.sixBoltBody: Rotor attached via 6 Torx bolts. Universal and robust.
brake.centerLockBody: Splined interface with a lockring. Faster installation, lighter, favored by Shimano/Road.

ratchet.title: Ratchet Engagement
ratchet.body: Higher tooth counts mean faster engagement, with less lag when you start pedaling.

freehub.title: Freehub Body Compatibility
freehub.body: HG vs MS vs XD vs XDR vs N3W? Check our detailed guide.

choose.title: Hub Selection Guide
choose.intro: Choosing the right hub is a balance between serviceability, performance, and compatibility.

jBend.title: 1. J-bend Hub
jBend.structure: Flange holes designed for spokes with a 90° bend (elbow).
jBend.advantages: Traditional design, easy to source replacements, convenient maintenance.
jBend.bestFor: Riders valuing universality and ease of future maintenance.

straightPull.title: 2. Straight-pull Hub
straightPull.structure: Flange holes designed for spokes that insert directly without bending.
straightPull.advantages: Stiffer structure, more even tension, high-performance aesthetic.
straightPull.bestFor: Racing or performance use seeking rigidity and weight savings.

holeCount.title: 3. Hole Count Selection
holeCount.lightweightBody: Lighter weight, strictly for road bikes and climbing sets. Requires higher spoke tension and stiffer rims.
holeCount.durabilityBody: More durable, suitable for MTB, heavy loads, or touring. Distributes stress across more spokes.
holeCount.principle: Hub hole count must match rim hole count exactly.

notes.title: Critical Notes
items: Hub type must match spoke type (J-bend to J-bend, SP to SP).
Hole count should be chosen based on the riding scenario: lightweight vs durability.
High-performance wheelsets often use straight-pull hubs with fewer holes; durable wheelsets often use J-bend hubs with more holes.
